title: Three days in Myrtle Beach with kids
summary: A relaxed plan with beach time, one big attraction a day and mini golf at night
description: A three-day Myrtle Beach itinerary for families: beach mornings, one big attraction per day, mini golf at night, and a backup plan for rain.
intro: The easiest way to wear out a family on the Grand Strand is to schedule too much. This plan keeps it to one main thing per day, with the beach as the default and mini golf as the evening ritual. Swap days around to suit the weather and your kids' ages.
Everything here is on our site, so you can tap through for addresses and details. Hours, prices and seasonal closures change, so check each listing's own page before you leave.

sections.h: Day 1: Settle in and keep it simple
p: Spend the morning on the sand while everyone gets used to being on vacation. In the afternoon, walk the Myrtle Beach Boardwalk, which is free, and ride the SkyWheel if the kids are tall enough to enjoy the view. Then pick one mini golf course within walking distance of your hotel. Captain Hook's, Pirate's Watch and Jungle Lagoon are all close to the oceanfront in Central Myrtle Beach.

Choose one: Ripley's Aquarium, WonderWorks or Alligator Adventure. Ripley's and WonderWorks are close to each other around Broadway at the Beach and the oceanfront, while Alligator Adventure is in North Myrtle Beach at Barefoot Landing. Do a big attraction in the morning, eat early, and give the kids a break by the pool or beach in the afternoon.
If your kids are younger, EdVenture Myrtle Beach is built for them and works well on a day that you would like to be less crowded.

sections.h: Day 3: Get on the water or go further
p: A dolphin cruise from Murrells Inlet or Little River is a good family option, and it adds variety. Sightings are common but never guaranteed, so set expectations with younger kids. If your family prefers land, Myrtle Beach State Park or Huntington Beach State Park have trails, a beach and in the case of Huntington Beach, alligators and shorebirds.

Finish with a second mini golf course on a different theme. The Professor Hacker's dinosaur courses and Mutiny Bay in North Myrtle Beach, or Gilligan's Island Funland in Surfside, make a change from the oceanfront.

Move the big attraction to the rainy day. WonderWorks, Ripley's, the Pinball Museum, Sky Zone and an escape room all work indoors. Our family and indoor page has the full list, and the rainy-day guide groups them by type.

list: Beach time is best in the morning and early evening. Midday sun and crowds peak together.
Book timed tickets and escape rooms ahead in summer.
Check height and age limits before you promise a ride or ropes course.
Remember the local beach rules on glass, alcohol, tents and dogs. They differ by town.
